newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTH AFRICA LIFTS MORATORIUM ON POLICE RECRUITMENT.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AFRICA LIFTS MORATORIUM ON POLICE RECRUITMENT.

text.p: Crime-scarred South Africa lifted a moratorium on new police recruits on Thursday, promising to spend almost 150 million rand ($33 million) on hiring both civilians and officers for priority policing areas.
"The moratorium on recruitment of police officers is lifted with immediate effect," police minister Sydney Mufamadi said in a statement issued at a Pretoria news briefing.
A total of 5,250 staff would be employed, of which roughly half Would be civilian employees in order to free up trained officers to work on the beat, he said.

The moratorium was imposed by the fledgling African National Congress-led government in August 1994 when Mufamadi was faced with integrating a white-oriented and splintered force loathed by blacks into a public-friendly police service.
President Nelson Mandela's government has also bewailed the levels of corruption and inefficiency in the force it inherited.
More than ofe in 10 members of South Africa's National Protection Service -- which looks after Mandela and his cabinet -- are facing charges ranging from rape and assault to murder.

Mufamadi, pointing to police statistics that about one-third of South Africa's 140,000 police officers do not have driving licences, and that 30,000 failed to complete even high school, said the new recruitment drive would target skilled personnel.

"We will not recruit for the sake of bolstering numbers... We will seek high academic performers (and) will not condone candidates who have criminal records," said South Africa's first black police minister.
The problem of crime among officers surfaced recently when ministers, President Mandela and Deputy President Thabo Mbeki were found to have suffered a rash of thefts from their homes.

While political violence has declined dramatically under Mandela's government, violent crime including rape, murder and car hijacks, has soared -- scaring off investment and tourists and is one of the main causes of an exodus of skilled people.

Mufamadi said the new recruits would be deployed in priority areas including the border unit, forensic science laboratory, firearms unit, family violence and child abuse unit and the anti-corruption division. The cost would be absorbed into his department's current budget allocation.
